B_cab_ratio_denominator.definition: Historical concurrent cabinet exceedance-hours above the per-cabinet P99 threshold
B_cab_ratio_denominator.reason: cab_p99_W is scaled by CAB_SCALE at lines 262-263 BEFORE B_cab_hist is computed at line 428. Therefore B_cab_hist changes with CAB_SCALE.

B_cab_ratio_numerator.definition: Simulation concurrent cabinet exceedance-hours above the per-cabinet P99 threshold
B_cab_ratio_numerator.reason: Same cab_p99_W (already scaled by CAB_SCALE) is used for the numerator.

CAB_SCALE_application.code: if CAB_SCALE != 1.00: cab_p99_W = {c: CAB_SCALE * v for c, v in cab_p99_W.items()}
CAB_SCALE_application.effect: Multiplies ALL per-cabinet P99 thresholds by CAB_SCALE. Applied once before B_cab_hist (line 428) and before all per-scenario B_cab_h computations (line 824).
CAB_SCALE_application.timing: After loading cabinet envelopes (lines 256-261) but before computing B_cab_hist (line 428) and before any per-scenario simulation (line 824).

CAB_SCALE_effect_on_ratio.direction: Higher CAB_SCALE -> higher thresholds -> fewer historical exceedance hours (lower B_cab_hist) AND fewer simulation exceedance hours (lower B_cab_h). The ratio B_cab_h/B_cab_hist changes nonlinearly depending on the relative sensitivity of historical vs simulation concurrent power to the threshold.
CAB_SCALE_effect_on_ratio.linearity: Nonlinear. Both numerator and denominator decrease, but at rates determined by different concurrent power profiles (historical job cohort vs synthetic scheduling).
CAB_SCALE_effect_on_ratio.correct_statement: CAB_SCALE changes both the B_cab numerator and denominator simultaneously. The ratio direction depends on empirical power distributions and cannot be stated without running the simulation.

B_ref_s_correct_role.definition: Node-level THERMAL incidence reference hours, computed from T_THR_PRIMARY (63.625 C)
B_ref_s_correct_role.note: B_ref_s is the thermal budget reference, paired with B_primary_h to form B_primary_ratio. It is NOT B_cab_hist. The prior plan claim that B_ref_s was the cabinet exceedance denominator was an incorrect variable identification.

prior_incorrect_claims_retracted: Amendment 2 stated that B_ref_s was the historical exceedance-hours denominator and was fixed at the base threshold. This confused B_ref_s (thermal, per-scenario, T_THR_PRIMARY-based) with B_cab_hist (cabinet, pre-simulation, varies with CAB_SCALE).

The empirical observation that B_ref_s=2449.93 is constant across CAB_SCALE for sc30 is correct but trivially explains nothing about the cabinet denominator: B_ref_s is invariant to CAB_SCALE because it depends only on T_THR_PRIMARY, not on cab_p99_W.

corrected_E1_statement.threshold_effect: CAB_SCALE multiplies each per-cabinet P99 threshold: Q_c_scaled = CAB_SCALE * Q_c_base.
corrected_E1_statement.denominator_effect: B_cab_hist (cabinet denominator) is recomputed after scaling. Higher CAB_SCALE -> higher threshold -> fewer historical exceedance hours -> lower B_cab_hist.
corrected_E1_statement.numerator_effect: B_cab_h (cabinet numerator) is recomputed after scaling. Higher CAB_SCALE -> higher threshold -> fewer simulation exceedance hours -> lower B_cab_h.
corrected_E1_statement.ratio_effect: Nonlinear. Cannot be asserted without empirical simulation output.
corrected_E1_statement.thermal_reference_unaffected: B_ref_s and S_ref_s (thermal node-level references) are unchanged by CAB_SCALE.

plan_action: Remove all assertions from the plan about whether the cabinet denominator is fixed or recomputed. State only: (1) CAB_SCALE multiplies per-cabinet P99 thresholds; (2) both B_cab_hist and B_cab_h are recomputed after scaling; (3) the B_cab_ratio is nonlinear in CAB_SCALE and requires empirical inspection.
